uncited: It sets itself apart from direct relighting methods by either replacing object shading based on scene correlations [Shading Replacement for Relighting](6346-shading-replacement-for-relighting.md) or integrating surface rendering principles into the volume rendering framework to model irradiance [Pano-NeRF](15013-pano-nerf.md).
**Irradiance-Radiance Coupling**: Radiance is treated as both a signal conveying lighting information and a light source illuminating other pixels [Pano-NeRF](15013-pano-nerf.md).
This increases observation counts for geometry and leverages irradiance-radiance attenuation for High Dynamic Range (HDR) reconstruction [Pano-NeRF](15013-pano-nerf.md).
**Surface-Volume Integration**: Methods may integrate surface rendering principles (BRDF, normals) into the volumetric framework [Pano-NeRF](15013-pano-nerf.md).
where $f_r$ is the BRDF, $\mathbf{n}$ is the surface normal, and $c_i(x, \omega_i)$ is the incoming radiance computed via volume rendering [Pano-NeRF](15013-pano-nerf.md).

**Shading Correlation**: In object insertion tasks, shading is inferred by correlating surface normals and shading values between the inserted object and the existing scene, avoiding explicit light source estimation [Shading Replacement for Relighting](6346-shading-replacement-for-relighting.md).

Pano-NeRF and Shading Replacement for Relighting further extend this by explicitly handling irradiance fields and shading correlations, respectively, to solve issues in sparse view synthesis and object compositing [Pano-NeRF](15013-pano-nerf.md, 6346-shading-replacement-for-relighting.md).
